design_summary.purpose: Adaptive aero control FPGA top level that combines a firmware-visible CSR/MMIO control plane with 128-bit model request/response streams, deterministic safety filtering, timeout supervision, fallback handling, and bounded actuator-command output.
design_summary.operating_model: Single synchronous clk domain with synchronous active-low rst_n reset. Firmware configures enable, clear_fault, sequence seed, timeouts, limits, fallback value, operating mode, and config_valid through the CSR window. When enabled and configured, the controller emits compact model requests, accepts streamed model responses, validates sequence/integrity/freshness, applies clamp and rate-limit policy, and updates a registered actuator output or safe fallback output. Faults can latch the design into a safe state until clear_fault and a clean re-enable sequence are observed.

external_interfaces.name: clk
external_interfaces.intent: System clock fanout for all submodules and registered state.

external_interfaces.name: rst_n
external_interfaces.intent: Synchronous active-low reset that initializes the controller to deterministic safe fallback behavior.

external_interfaces.name: ctrl_reg_rdata
external_interfaces.intent: Firmware-visible CSR/MMIO read data returned from decoded register space.

external_interfaces.name: model_req_valid
external_interfaces.intent: Outbound request-stream valid from RTL toward the external software/firmware transport path.

external_interfaces.name: model_req_ready
external_interfaces.intent: Inbound ready from the external transport path for request acceptance.

external_interfaces.name: model_req_data
external_interfaces.intent: Compact outbound request packet carrying request sequence, setpoint/current-velocity placeholder, external handle/index, mode flags, and checksum/parity.

external_interfaces.name: model_resp_valid
external_interfaces.intent: Inbound response-stream valid from the external software/firmware transport path.

external_interfaces.name: model_resp_ready
external_interfaces.intent: Outbound ready from RTL accepting response packets.

external_interfaces.name: model_resp_data
external_interfaces.intent: Compact inbound response packet carrying response sequence, command value(s), validity flags, and checksum/parity.

external_interfaces.name: actuator_cmd_out
external_interfaces.intent: Registered, deterministic bounded actuator command output.

external_interfaces.name: fault_status_out
external_interfaces.intent: Compact fault and fallback status bits for firmware observability.

module_architecture.name: adaptive_aero_control_top
module_architecture.role: Top-level FPGA control plane and data-path integrator.
responsibilities: Own the firmware-visible CSR/MMIO window and expose a real firmware-facing register interface with address, write-data, read-data, transaction-valid/write-enable, and ready/response semantics.
Integrate request packetization, response parsing, validation, watchdog supervision, clamp and rate limiting, fallback control, and registered actuator/status outputs.
Preserve the top-level contract that no geometry arrays, flow fields, or surrogate tensors are exposed at the top level.
Host compact technology-neutral staging memory for bounded request/response/history telemetry buffering when needed for FPGA mapping.
interface_notes: Top-level ports are limited to clk, rst_n, compact control registers, 128-bit request/response streams, actuator_cmd_out, and fault_status_out.
All outputs are driven by real RTL ownership at the top level or through explicitly owned child submodule outputs; no required top-level output is left to an undriven or child-input-only connection.

Request/response direction follows the mandatory transport contract: model_req_valid and model_req_data are RTL outputs, model_req_ready is an input; model_resp_valid and model_resp_data are inputs, model_resp_ready is an output.
ownership_notes: Owns the overall design contract and top-level interconnect.
Owns the exposed top-level scalar-equivalent I/O budget, which remains below 256.
Owns the external-facing firmware/MMIO contract and the streaming transport contract.

module_architecture.name: adaptive_aero_control_csr
module_architecture.role: Firmware-visible CSR/MMIO register window with decode, readback, write strobes, status multiplexing, and configuration extraction.
responsibilities: Implement the compact firmware-visible MMIO register map.
Decode writes into configuration fields and expose readable status fields.

Provide configuration registers for enable, clear_fault, sequence seed, request timeout threshold, response age threshold, actuator minimum clamp, actuator maximum clamp, actuator rate limit, fallback command value, operating mode, and configuration-valid bit.

Provide status readback for FSM state, accepted/request/response sequence numbers, timeout counter, stale reject counter, clamp event counter, fault cause code, fallback active flag, and fault-latched flag.
Make every declared register reachable through RTL decode; inaccessible state is not treated as software-visible.
interface_notes: Consumes the CSR address/data/write/read handshake from the top level and produces decoded configuration outputs plus readback data and response handshake flags.
Serves as the sole owner of CSR configuration outputs within the hierarchy.
ownership_notes: Owns cfg_enable, cfg_clear_fault, cfg_sequence_seed, cfg_request_timeout_threshold, cfg_response_age_threshold, cfg_actuator_min_clamp, cfg_actuator_max_clamp, cfg_actuator_rate_limit, cfg_fallback_command_value, cfg_operating_mode, and cfg_config_valid.
Owns CSR read-data and CSR response timing signals at the hierarchy boundary.
Provides the register_contract implementation through RTL decode.

module_architecture.name: adaptive_aero_control_stream
module_architecture.role: External model transport, request packet assembly, response parsing, sequencing, and handshake supervision.
responsibilities: Generate outbound request packets only when enabled, configured, not busy, and not fault-latched.
Assemble 128-bit request packets carrying request sequence number, setpoint/current-velocity placeholder, geometry handle or external payload identifier, mode flags, and checksum/parity.
Receive 128-bit response packets from the external transport and validate sequence integrity, freshness, integrity, and age against timeout thresholds.
Reject malformed frames, mismatched sequence numbers, stale responses, duplicated responses, and responses arriving after threshold expiration.
Update internal accepted-command staging registers only after a valid response passes parser checks; downstream actuator driving remains gated by safety policy.
Expose status hooks for request issuance, response acceptance, stale reject activity, timeout activity, and fallback causes.
interface_notes: Implements the mandatory stream direction contract with request-valid/data as outputs, request-ready as input, response-valid/data as inputs, and response-ready as output.
Owns the request/response transaction state machine and the visible FSM/state counters.
Provides accepted_command_word to the safety filter as a bounded staging word rather than directly driving the actuator.
ownership_notes: Owns status_fsm_state, status_last_accepted_sequence, status_last_request_sequence, status_last_response_sequence, status_timeout_counter, status_stale_reject_counter, status_clamp_event_counter, status_fault_cause_code, status_fallback_active, status_fault_latched, model_req_valid, model_req_data, model_resp_ready, and accepted_command_word.
Owns the external request/response sequencing and timeout supervision logic.
May use bounded memory for staging and telemetry snapshots, but does not flatten payload buffering into top-level registers.

module_architecture.name: adaptive_aero_control_safety
module_architecture.role: Safety filtering, clamp and rate limit enforcement, fallback control, and fault-latching logic.
responsibilities: Apply programmable minimum and maximum clamp limits to each command component.
Apply a programmable rate limit relative to the last applied command.
Record clamp events in status when clamping occurs.
Apply a clamped command only if it remains within safe policy; otherwise transition to fallback.
Assert fallback on policy violations, invalid configuration, timeout-derived conditions, or other fault conditions.
Drive deterministic safe fallback output in RESET, IDLE, FALLBACK, and fault-latched states.
Produce compact fault/status output bits for stale reject, timeout, clamp event, fault latch, fallback active, and configuration invalid.
interface_notes: Consumes accepted_command_word from the stream parser and configuration/status context from the CSR and stream blocks.
Drives actuator_cmd_out and fault_status_out as registered outputs only on clock edges.
Maintains output determinism and avoids combinational loops with request/response stages.
ownership_notes: Owns actuator_cmd_out and fault_status_out at the hierarchy boundary.
Owns the safety policy application that bounds the command before output update.
Owns fallback selection behavior and fault-latched hold behavior.

interface_summary.intent: Firmware-visible CSR/MMIO decode and status readback with configuration extraction.
Provide control-plane configuration used for request issuance, sequencing, timeout supervision, and configuration gating.
Provide safety-policy configuration and clean-clear control.
Expose controller state, counters, and fault/fallback status to firmware-visible registers.
Provide parser outcomes and accepted command staging for safety filtering and output selection.
Emit compact outbound request packets toward the software/firmware transport path when enabled, configured, and ready.
Provide handshake readiness for request acceptance.
Deliver compact inbound response packets for validation and command staging.
Acknowledge response acceptance using the required RTL-output ready signal.
Drive registered bounded actuator command and compact fault/fallback status.

data_flow_summary: Firmware writes configuration through the CSR/MMIO window; decoded configuration becomes the sole source of control-plane settings.

When enabled, configured, and not fault-latched, the stream block emits a 128-bit request packet containing a request sequence number, compact external payload reference, mode flags, and integrity field.
The external software/firmware transport returns a compact 128-bit response packet; the stream block accepts it only when response_valid and response_ready handshake succeeds.

The response parser checks sequence match, freshness, integrity, and age; valid responses update an accepted-command staging word while malformed, stale, duplicated, or late responses increment counters and can trigger fallback or fault-latch behavior.
The safety block clamps and rate-limits the accepted command relative to the last applied command, records clamp events, and only registers actuator output changes that satisfy policy.
RESET, IDLE, FALLBACK, and FAULT_LATCH states drive safe fallback outputs, while explicit clear_fault and a clean configuration/enable sequence are required to exit a latched fault state.

clock_reset_summary.clocking: Single synchronous clock domain on clk. All control outputs, status registers, stream handshakes, and actuator/fault outputs are registered on clk edges.
clock_reset_summary.reset_behavior: rst_n is synchronous active-low and initializes the controller into deterministic safe fallback state. Reset forces safe outputs, clears or initializes sequence/status state deterministically, and avoids combinational dependence between request, response, and output paths.

integration_notes: The design is FPGA-oriented and may instantiate technology-neutral staging memory or inferred block RAM for minimal request/response/history buffering; bulk payload storage is not flattened into registers.
Sky130 hard macros are not used in FPGA synthesis.
The top-level module remains compact and does not expose geometry arrays, flow fields, or surrogate tensors; only compact handles and sequence metadata are carried in-stream.
The external model computation is assumed to run in software, GPU, or firmware; the RTL supports transparent CPU-reference operation without depending on internal surrogate computation.

The memory contract is descriptive only here: any later ASIC port must use the specified sky130_sram_1kbyte_1rw1r_32x256_8 hard macro and stop at the memory-collateral gate unless the required collateral is available.
consistency_notes: No hierarchy, ports, or filenames may differ from digital_spec_json.
